about: The record of every sound effect and piece of music in public/assets/audio/ (D-28, D-45): where each came from and under what licence. 'sources', 'elevenlabs', 'lyria', 'sfx' and 'music' are written by hand and read by scripts/art/audio.ts and scripts/art/music.ts; 'outputs' is filled in by those scripts. Downloads live in the git-ignored art/cache/kenney-audio/, generated candidates in the git-ignored art/out/audio/ and art/out/music/. How to re-run: docs/assets/AUDIO.md.

elevenlabs.service: ElevenLabs sound effects (POST /v1/sound-generation), on the owner's paid account

elevenlabs.licence: Generated for this project on the owner's paid ElevenLabs plan, whose terms give the output to the account holder and allow commercial use. No third party holds rights in it; it is shared here as part of the game. AI-generated.

lyria.service: Google Lyria through the Gemini API's Interactions endpoint, on the owner's Gemini key (as Starman Control)
lyria.licence: Generated for this project with Google's Lyria; Google claims no ownership of generated output (Gemini API terms). Every piece carries Google's inaudible SynthID watermark. AI-generated. No prompt names an artist, a composer or a work.
lyria.style: An original instrumental score cue for a grounded, melancholy science-fiction game set on a remote research station on a planet of a dim red dwarf star. One consistent palette across the whole score: warm analogue synthesiser pads, low strings (cellos and double basses), sparse felt piano, and cold, glassy, bell-like textures. Mixed to sit quietly under dialogue and sound effects: restrained and spacious, no sudden loud hits, no drops. Instrumental only: no vocals, no singing, no humming, no spoken words, no choir.

music.subject: The main theme. About ninety seconds long. Slow, about 66 BPM, in D minor: a dying red star, hope under dread. It opens on a low drone and a distant glassy shimmer; a simple, memorable melody of a few notes on felt piano enters over slow pads and low strings, and a solo cello answers it; the strings swell gently towards a warm major chord, then fall back to the drone. Steady to the end, without a fade-out, so it can loop.
music.pickNote: Chosen by Claude from Gemini 3.1 Pro's timeline description of every candidate (24 October 2026): the one closest to the brief with no brass and no choir. The owner may overrule by changing 'pick'.

music.what: The night shift before the attack (loop)
music.subject: Calm, uneasy ambient music for a station at three in the morning, on the night shift. About two minutes long. Very slow, about 60 BPM, in A minor. Long, evolving synthesiser pads and a soft low string drone, sparse felt piano notes far apart, the faint ring of distant glassy bells, a quiet pulse like machinery deep in the walls. No drums, no woodwinds, no swells and no climax: it stays quiet and even from start to finish. Calm, but something is not quite right. Without a fade-out, so it can loop.
music.pickNote: Chosen by Claude from Gemini 3.1 Pro's timeline description of every candidate (24 October 2026): the one closest to the brief with no brass and no choir. The owner may overrule by changing 'pick'.

music.what: After the lights go, walking to Control (loop)
music.subject: Tense, quiet music after the station's lights go out, walking through dark corridors towards the control room. About ninety seconds long. Slow, about 70 BPM, in C minor. A low, steady pulse on deep synthesiser, taut low strings with slow tremolo, dissonant glassy textures that rise and fall, a muted low thud like a distant heartbeat. Suspense that never breaks: no big melody, no climax. Even throughout, without a fade-out, so it can loop.
music.pickNote: Chosen by Claude from Gemini 3.1 Pro's timeline description of every candidate (24 October 2026): the one closest to the brief with no brass and no choir. The owner may overrule by changing 'pick'.

music.subject: Driving, dark electronic music for tense, fast action in a dark station. About two minutes long. Fast, about 124 BPM, in E minor. A pulsing analogue synthesiser bass in steady sixteenth notes, tight electronic drums, cold arpeggiated synthesisers and glassy stabs, with a small section of cellos and violas playing short, repeated notes underneath. Minimal, relentless and mechanical, like machinery that will not stop; tense and determined, never epic or triumphant. No brass, no horns, no choir, no cymbal crashes, no big melody. The same intensity throughout, without a fade-in or an ending, so it can loop.
music.pickNote: Chosen by Claude from Gemini 3.1 Pro's timeline description of every candidate (24 October 2026): the one closest to the brief with no brass and no choir. The owner may overrule by changing 'pick'.

music.what: The bridge, the escape and the ending (plays once)
music.subject: Music for the escape and the ending: a small ship lifts away from the dark station and its dim red star. About two minutes long. Slow, about 64 BPM, in D minor turning to F major. It begins with felt piano and pads alone; a simple, slow melody on solo cello enters; the low strings and warm pads rise to a broad, hopeful, resolved statement; then it settles on a long, quiet major chord and fades gently to silence. Melancholic, hopeful and resolved, never triumphant.
music.pickNote: Chosen by Claude from Gemini 3.1 Pro's timeline description of every candidate (24 October 2026): the one closest to the brief with no brass and no choir. The owner may overrule by changing 'pick'.
